name: EZIO4O
description: A plug-in load controller with 4 relays that switch AC or DC loads on Insteon or X10 commands.

verification.note: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) assigns 0x07/0x08 to the EZIO4O; the EZIOxx Advanced Details give 0x07/0x02 for EZIO as a whole. The catalog uses 0x07/0x08, the model's own entry.
The EZIOxx Advanced Details cover the whole EZIOxx line, from inputs-only to outputs-only models, and warn that a model may not support every command.
The Quick-Start Guide EZIO4O—Model #5010J—4-Relay Load Controller links relay N by tapping the SET button N times; numbering the relays as groups 1 to 4 follows that.

steps.text: Choose a power outlet close to the loads to be controlled, away from moisture. Outdoors, use an approved weatherproof enclosure.
Connect the loads to the relay terminals: Rx_NO (normally open), RxCM (common) and Rx_NC (normally closed) for relays 1 to 4.
Plug the EZIO4O into an AC outlet.
steps.expect: LED may flash rapidly a few times, turns on and off for about 1 second, then glows steadily

steps.text: Put the controller in linking mode by holding the button that will control the relays until it shows linking mode, 4 to 10 seconds depending on the controller.
steps.expect: Controller LED blinks or a light connected to it flashes

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED turns off; the controller's LED or a light connected to it flashes

steps.text: Tap the SET button once for relay 1, twice for relay 2, and so on.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.

notes: The EZIO4O links as a responder.

To link a snapshot of all the relays as they are, for the controller to recall, skip the taps: the Quick-Start Guide EZIO4O—Model #5010J—4-Relay Load Controller gives this first, and linking one relay as the other way.

X10: relays 1 to 4 answer X10 units 1 to 4, and the device takes a whole house code. To enable X10, press and hold the SET button for about 4 seconds (the LED blinks slowly) and send an On from an X10 controller; the LED stops blinking. An Off disables it. The Quick-Start Guide EZIO4O—Model #5010J—4-Relay Load Controller sends one On; the EZIOxx Advanced Details choose the house code on the X10 controller first and send 3 On commands in succession. This note follows the Quick-Start Guide EZIO4O—Model #5010J—4-Relay Load Controller.

steps.text: Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the controller, for group 0.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
Tap the SET button once, for relay 1.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
Wait for the Hub to report the new link.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request.
steps.expect: The device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version

steps.text: Have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.

notes: This links the Hub's group 0 to the device as a responder, for relay 1; the device makes no link back to the Hub, since this profile lists no group it controls.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's linking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, ID Request and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Put the controller in unlinking mode, as its own instructions say.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED flashes briefly, then turns on solidly; the controller's LED turns on solidly

steps.text: Unlink the device from every controller it is linked to.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Have the Hub start unlinking for group 0 (Start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF).
Press and hold the SET button for 3 to 4 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: LED flashes briefly, then turns on solidly

steps.text: Wait for the Hub to report that the link is gone.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's unlinking steps and the standard Insteon command Start ALL-Linking; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Each relay is a switch rated 0.5 A at 30 V DC or 120 V AC, with normally open, common and normally closed terminals (Rx_NO, RxCM, Rx_NC). Timers can pulse a relay from 1 second to 255 minutes; setting them takes software.
The Quick-Start Guide EZIO4O—Model #5010J—4-Relay Load Controller applies to firmware 2.0 and above.
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)
